ec603e82ea: Play all six strings. Middle finger on string 6, index on string 5, ring finger on string 1, wrist a little lower.
f07eb04097: Only one finger different from C: the ring finger moves from string 5 to string 3, index and middle stay put.
c393fa084f: Play strings 4 to 1 only. The index finger lies flat across strings 1 and 2 at fret 1. The full barre F waits until Chapter 8.
b75ed2889b: Play strings 4 to 1 only, three fingers in a small triangle.
ab9be78dc1: Play all six strings. Same shape as Am, moved one string toward string 6.
ddbe6ce8ca: Three fingers side by side at fret 2, letting string 1 ring.
28d44b532c: The index finger barres strings 5 to 1 at fret 2, skipping string 6.
8ff5721177: The index finger presses all six strings at fret 1, with the E shape on top.

d725252056: Strum down once on every beat; your hand comes back up on the half beat, ready again.
8399635691: Down on the beat, up on the half beat, eight even strokes.
672de6f57c: The downstroke on beat 3 is left out, so the accent moves forward. Say it: down, down-up, up-down-up.
d93d96ef45: Each beat splits into four, and your hand swings twice as fast. Keep the downstrokes on the beat and add upstrokes on the offbeats for a finer, more driving groove.
adcdfa3f55: Play a bass note on beats 1 and 3 (boom) and strum the treble strings on beats 2 and 4 (chick-a). Move the second bass note to the next string and the accompaniment starts to walk.
cdf15ce6ec: Strong, weak, weak: a bass note on beat 1, treble strums on beats 2 and 3. Waltzes and lots of slow songs use this accompaniment.
9f81393708: Add an upstroke after each waltz "chick" and triple time starts to flow too.
03e0d77789: Six eighth notes per bar in two big beats: boom-chick-a, boom-chick-a, like a gently rocking cradle.
baaca7ed4a: On beats 2 and 4, "slap" the strings with the side of your right palm or fingers for a snare-like "chk". Relax the left hand at the same time to mute the strings.
7b33693e09: Three eighth notes in every beat. Common in blues and old-style love songs: slow and deep in feeling.
3230338f34: Holds the tuning pegs; the brand logo usually sits here.
2c179fc6f4: Hold the strings and tune them by tightening or loosening. Good pegs have precise gears and stay in tune; sealed (oil-filled) and open types are common.
1145946bfa: Sets the spacing of the six strings. The harder the material, the less vibration is lost; bone, plastic and Tusq are common.
46c78fa5d1: Where the left hand presses the strings, usually rosewood, ebony or maple. The harder the wood, the better it wears.
d2c918d181: The metal strips on the fretboard. Press between two frets and the string length is fixed at the fret in front, giving a steady pitch.
0299335cab: Marked at frets 3, 5, 7, 9 and 12 so you can find your place quickly; fret 12 has two dots and is exactly an octave above the open string.
17c8206c1e: Joins the headstock to the body, with a steel truss rod inside to adjust its bow.
eeda27500e: The wooden board on the front of the body, the main source of the tone. The top vibrates and turns the strings' energy into the sound you hear.
a604f3137a: The air inside the body moves in and out here as it resonates, sending the sound out.
6c78ce7d15: The decoration around the sound hole, which also reinforces its edge; made of plastic, wood or shell.
ff6e8f6079: Protects the top from pick scratches when you strum.
2f709c104c: Glued to the top, it takes the pull of the strings and passes their vibration to the top.
4702e1a54e: Where the vibrating string ends, passing the vibration into the bridge and top. Its height sets the action (the distance between strings and fretboard).
3a7807bf88: Small pins that hold the string ends in the bridge; you only pull them out to change strings.
4acdb7169a: The edging around the body, which protects the joins and shows how fine the workmanship is.
8d6f72d78e: The sides and back of the body, which form the sound box with the top and shape the depth and sustain of the bass.
